recentEvents.text: DECISION REQUIRED Herzeg-Bosna · 6 Apr 1992 What Is Herceg-Bosna? PRESIDENTIAL RESPONSE Croat republic — follow Zagreb HISTORICAL DEFAULT This is the historically attested choice. You are free to choose any option. Herceg-Bosna is a Croat political entity. We will control our territory along the old Banovina borders. Zagreb provides arms, officers, and purpose. The Bosniaks will become adversaries. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina / Herzeg-Bosna alliance -0.15 Herzeg-Bosna morale +5 Herzeg-Bosna Patron Confidence +15 Herzeg-Bosna Int'l Standing -10 Herzeg-Bosna Internal Cohesion +10 Herzeg-Bosna Military Credibility +5 United front with ARBiH We are Croats and Bosnians. Our fight is against Greater Serbia, alongside our allies. Zagreb will be furious. Tudjman may cut support. But the combined front against the VRS will be formidable. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina / Herzeg-Bosna alliance +0.15 Herzeg-Bosna morale -3 Herzeg-Bosna Patron Confidence -25 Herzeg-Bosna Int'l Standing +15 Herzeg-Bosna Internal Cohesion -10 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Internal Cohesion +5 Cooperate publicly, prepare quietly Fight the Serbs together. Build Croat institutions behind the scenes. Zagreb tolerates it. The alliance holds — for now. When it breaks, and it will, the betrayal will cost you double. Herzeg-Bosna morale +2 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina / Herzeg-Bosna alliance -0.05 Herzeg-Bosna Patron Confidence +5 Herzeg-Bosna Internal Cohesion -5 SITUATION Zagreb is on the line. Your patron's directive is clear: Herceg-Bosna exists to secure Croat territory in Bosnia, with a view toward eventual unification with Croatia. But on the ground, your HVO fights alongside the ARBiH against Serb forces. Some of your commanders — notably Kljuic — argue the Croat future lies in a unified Bosnia, not a separate statelet. Your patron disagrees. Choose your path: it will define your alliances, your wars, and your fate at the negotiating table. STAFF ASSESSMENT Herceg-Bosna leadership gains patron alignment and clearer institutional cohesion by following Zagreb, but the choice makes cooperation with Sarajevo more fragile. Each constituent people would govern areas where they form a majority. The split would give Bosniaks and Serbs 44% each, with Croats receiving 12%. All three sides initially agreed in Lisbon, but the deal is fragile — rejection by any party will signal that partition cannot be achieved through negotiation alone.
